title: Wholesale check
intro: A sanity check on the wholesale layer in the flow model: do the biggest wholesalers in each country sell roughly what the layer says? The dashboard layer in the table is live from the flow model. The company figures come from a separate research run in October 2026, and we re-opened a selection of the sources ourselves.
findings: No country shows a wholesale layer that looks too high. For Hungary, Germany, the UK, Spain and Italy the biggest named wholesalers plausibly carry 40–95% of the layer, which is what a concentrated trade should show.
Hungary has the closest independent match: a bond document puts passenger-tyre wholesale at about 70% of the market, against 73% in the dashboard.
France, Switzerland, Belgium and Denmark cannot be tested yet, because the named wholesalers publish too little. The gaps are listed below.

Austria (updated 26 Oct 2026) is plausible but low confidence. With the sales team's 0.6M for Reifen NL, the named domestic wholesalers add up to about 1.35–1.75M against the 1.82M layer, 74–96%. Without that figure they add up to about 0.8–1.3M. Reifen NL is one unpublished figure, so treat the result as provisional.

Poland (updated 28 Oct 2026) is plausible but low confidence. Handlopex, Inter Cars and JMK together carry about 31–62% of the 10.5M layer, which is mostly imported non-pool tyres; the layer rests on Poland's customs figure for China and two estimates, so the check cannot confirm it.
The Netherlands cannot be tested from company data, and may be pointing at understated import and re-export flows. That is a question for the model, not a finding.
Nothing in the model was changed by this check. It adds evidence, caveats and corrections only.

corrections.t: Netherlands: a mistake in the research brief
corrections.x: The brief given to the research run described the Dutch wholesale layer as including re-exports. It does not: the dashboard's 6.42M is domestic, after taking off the 2.41M that Dutch wholesalers send abroad. The report's verdict that the NL figure was “far off, too low” rests on that wrong description and is withdrawn. What company data can say about the Netherlands is shown in its own block.
Bond International is an independent family company; only Micheldever is owned by a manufacturer (Sumitomo, since 2017). The earlier note calling both “independent” is corrected on the card.

The research run reported 16.8 million tyres handled and one tyre every 3.5 seconds. The two Bond pages we opened say one tyre every six seconds and give 2024 turnover of £417M. The new estimate is 5–8M, and the 16.8M is not used.

corrections.t: Austria: how your colleague's list was sorted
corrections.x: Wholesale: AUTO PLUS and Reifen NL. Buying groups (independent member companies that pool their purchases): Point S, Top Reifen Team and EFR. BestDrive (Continental), Euromaster (Michelin), Forstinger and Lucky Car are chains or franchise networks that buy centrally, so they stay in the retail layer, where they already were. Car dealers: Porsche Inter Auto and Pappas. “BMW dealer” is generic, so we added the two largest BMW/MINI groups the research found, Denzel and Unterberger. Please confirm which one was meant.

The research run gave Point S's “about 20%” as a current claim. The only dated source we opened (2015) calls 20% a medium-term target and gives 17% as the actual consumer share. It is not used as a measured share.

Point S: 60+ locations (website, per the research run), 80+ (a member site) and 100 (2022 UTA release). BestDrive: 50+ workshops against about 60 locations. Porsche Inter Auto: over 50 dealerships (its employer profile, checked), 45 (research run) and over 40 sites (LinkedIn). Pappas: 21 sites (research run) against 33 branches in 2015 (Autohaus, checked). Denzel revenue: €1.165bn against more than €1.4bn.

Distri Cash 6.0M against 6.5M (and 5.5M in 2022); NEX 2.5M and €200M+ against 3.6M and €290.4M; Göggel €490M against €256M; Best4Tires about €600M against €508M; Bond 11 distribution centres against five.

method: The test: add up what the biggest wholesalers say they sell and compare it with the wholesale layer in the flow model. If they alone exceeded the layer, the layer would be too low. If they covered a tiny share of a layer that should be concentrated, it might be too high.

It is a sanity check, not a measurement. Company figures cover all tyre types (cars, trucks, motorbikes, agricultural), include exports and some own retail, and use different years. So they are ceilings for domestic passenger-car wholesale, not exact matches.
Where only revenue is known, tyres are derived at €60–100 a tyre. That range is wide on purpose.

evidence.x: Reifen NL at 0.6M lifts the named group from about 0.8–1.3M to 1.35–1.75M. That leaves 0.07–0.47M of the 1.82M unexplained, instead of 0.5–1.0M. The remainder could be foreign wholesalers (Interpneu, Delticom's trade arm), buying-group central stock or small regional distributors. No source publishes how concentrated Austrian wholesale is.

Reifen NL would be about as large as the floor of Auto Plus, yet it publishes no size and the company was registered only in Aug 2024. That is possible if it is a long-standing business under a new legal entity, but it is one unpublished figure. If it buys from other wholesalers, the sum above counts those tyres twice.

The research run's earlier reading, that the evidence pointed to about 1.0–1.4M if foreign wholesalers and buying-group stock do not count, assumed Reifen NL was small. It no longer holds if the 0.6M is right.

Point S says it holds about 20% of the market (its website, per the research run; not re-opened). The only dated source we opened, Auto & Wirtschaft of 1 Sep 2015, gives a traditional consumer-segment share of 17%, 60 locations and 50 shareholders, and calls 20% a medium-term target. We do not use 20% as a measured share. The page also lists 2026 events in its sidebar, so the date should be checked against the original.

Lucky Car: 62 locations and revenue just under €80M in 2025, up from about €70M (Leadersnet, 24 Mar 2026). It took over 24 former A.T.U sites and grew from €45M to €70M in 2024 (Leadersnet, 31 Mar 2025). Porsche Inter Auto's employer profile says “über 50 Autohäuser” in Austria. Pappas: an Autohaus item of 22 Jan 2016 gave 33 branches in seven companies.

gaps: Reifen NL: only the sales team's figure. Ask the team for its basis (own sales, a customer list or market intelligence) and whether it includes vans and light trucks.
Auto Plus has no audited volume. The Austrian company register (Firmenbuch) accounts for AUTO PLUS Fahrzeugzubehör GmbH and Reifen NL GmbH are the next best source.
No published figure for how concentrated Austrian wholesale is.
Delticom's trade arm and Interpneu: no Austria-specific volume.
Top Reifen Team, EFR, Forstinger's revenue and Euromaster's partner count come from the research run only; the pages could not be reached by our page reader.

The layer is two thirds imports (8.0M non-pool imports less 3.5M re-export), so the check only says the named firms do not contradict it: the rest would be smaller regional wholesalers and importers of record, including online sellers' own import arms. evidence.x: Oponeo, an online retailer, sold 4,259.12 thousand tyres in Poland in 2024 (opened and checked) and, per the research run, 4,728.79 thousand in 2025 (not re-opened); about 31% of the 15.99M market. It buys from manufacturers and wholesalers and belongs to the online channel, not the wholesale layer.

The CEO of PSO, a Kraków wholesaler, wrote that a few wholesalers remain from several dozen, the two largest each selling well above 2M tyres a year and the others roughly 0.7–1.5M. That fits Handlopex at about 3M but names no second large wholesaler, and it is seven years old.

Part of the layer is non-pool imports, 8.0M by the flow. Poland reports 7.03M car tyres imported from China in 2025 (WITS / Comtrade, quoted by the research run, not re-opened). Some of it is imported by online sellers' own arms (Enis is the exclusive Polish distributor of Austone), which the named wholesalers do not cover.

gaps: Inter Cars' tyre volumes are not published separately (Polish sales PLN 8.12bn across all products).
No second large wholesaler is named, and PSO (Kraków), Auto Partner and Moto-Profil have no published tyre volume.
The layer rests on the 8.0M import estimate; Eurostat Comext data by partner or a Europool non-pool figure would test it.
